title: When Does Logit Lens Fail? Identifying Layers Where Token Probability Prediction Is Unreliable

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with a gap: knowing failure boundaries of logit lens is useful for preventing misinterpretation, but it is more of a methods calibration than a direct safety impact.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Logit lens is straightforward to implement in TransformerLens. Computing KL divergence and token ranks at each layer is accessible. Comparing tuned lens adds modest complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: apply logit lens at every layer, compute two metrics, plot transition curves. Clear deliverable with minimal ambiguity. 500 prompts across 3 models is feasible in 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: This question has been largely addressed. The tuned lens paper (Belrose et al.) systematically documents logit lens failures across models and layers, proposes the tuned lens as a solution, and tests on models up to 20B parameters. Additional work explicitly documents when logit lens is deceptive. The proposed study would replicate known findings rather than generate new insights.

evidence.source: Eliciting Latent Predictions with the Tuned Lens (arXiv 2303.08112)
evidence.finding: The tuned lens paper explicitly documents logit lens failures on models like BLOOM and GPT Neo, shows it fails to elicit plausible predictions, and introduces the tuned lens as a fix for representational drift.

evidence.source: The Logit Lens Can Be Deceptive (Sonia Joseph, 2024)
evidence.finding: Explicitly documents when logit lens outputs are misleading, noting that information may be present but encoded in formats the logit lens cannot interpret.

evidence.source: Structure and Interpretation of Deep Networks (SIDN)
evidence.finding: Provides systematic comparison of lensing methods across layers and models, documenting reliability boundaries.
